text:
morgan: New customer stuck during quickstart. They ran the Docker sample from WSL2 on a company laptop using an always-on corporate VPN and saw intermittent failures: first call times out, second call succeeds, then onboarding banner shows 'Billing required' which confused them.

morgan: Command they ran (WSL2):
```
docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_trial_XXX redwood/quickstart:latest node index.js
```

morgan: Collated log snippets from customer:
```
[12:01:00] ERROR request id=1 error=connect ETIMEDOUT
[12:01:01] INFO sdk retrying (attempt 1) id=1
[12:01:02] INFO request id=1 status=200 OK
[12:01:10] ERROR repeated failures detected, showing billing banner
```

devon: VPN split-tunnel + WSL2 networking can route Docker traffic differently depending on whether the host resolver or container resolver is used, leading to transient timeouts. Not a billing issue.

support-bot: Workspace `maple-studios` is on trial; trial has low concurrency and a small request quota. But the customer's pattern is timeouts, not 4xx/5xx. Our onboarding banner logic currently treats repeated failures (timeouts, 5xx, 4xx) the same and surfaces a generic billing message.

morgan: customer also reported that running the quickstart directly on Windows CMD (outside WSL) passed consistently, so it seems WSL2+VPN is the differentiator.

infra-bot: Known flaky combo: WSL2 DNS + certain VPN clients cause intermittent DNS resolution failures inside containers. Ticket INFRA-3702 tracks a container networking doc we should add.

devon: Quick user unblock suggestions we gave:
- Run sample on host (works).
- If they must use WSL, try `--network=host` on Linux host (not available on Docker Desktop for Windows) or disable VPN split-tunnel for dev traffic.
- Configure Docker to use host DNS by adding "dns": ["8.8.8.8"] to daemon.json temporarily (documented with caveat).

morgan: Customer can't disable VPN due to company policy. We offered a hosted devbox instead and they accepted.

support-bot: Created support case and linked infra note: INFRA-3702 and DOCS-1010 (WSL2 & VPN troubleshooting). Also added onboard note clarifying that "billing banner" is a generic indicator and to check network/TLS/timeout causes first.

devon: Product/SDK items:
- Make the onboarding banner more specific: differentiate between network timeouts and billing/quota signals. Text suggestion: "Repeated request failures detected. If you see network timeouts or DNS errors, try running outside VPN/WSL or consult the WSL2+VPN troubleshooting guide. If you see 4xx/5xx errors, billing/quota may be the cause."
- SDK telemetry: attach failure reason (timeout vs 4xx) to the banner trigger so we don't mislead customers.

morgan: Agreed. Also update quickstart README with a short WSL2 note and the hosted devbox option for enterprise-locked laptops.

onboard-bot: Note added to workspace maple-studios: "offer hosted devbox; add WSL2+VPN troubleshooting; change onboarding banner to reduce billing confusion".

morgan: Customer completed onboarding using the hosted devbox and we closed the support ticket after drafting docs. Thanks all :clap:
